You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

2. Demo 2 input 25x25 has two motif instances at upper-left (approx rows 2–19, cols 3–10) and right (rows 9–19, cols 15–22). Output 4x8:
`[[0,8,0,0,0,0,8,8],[8,8,8,8,0,8,8,8],[0,0,8,0,0,0,0,8],[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,8]]`
3. Demo 3 input 22x22 has two motif instances, upper-left (rows 3–10, cols 3–8) and lower-right (rows 12–19, cols 14–19). Output 2x6:
`[[8,8,8,0,8,8],[0,0,8,0,0,0]]`

Output dimensions vary (3x7, 4x8, 2x6), apparently tied to a motif/component footprint, not a fixed output size. Need carefully compare component color/shape layers and identify which feature encodes the mask. Do not assume output is simply locations of color 3 or a raw damaged patch.

## Test instance salient data
24x25. Three visible motif-like regions: complex left at rows 4–11 cols 1–10, complex upper-right at rows 2–11 cols 14–22, and small lower-left panel rows 12–14 cols 2–9. Colors include 1,2,3,4,6. Test submissions all wrong.

1. 5x9 with manually guessed 3-pattern mask.

Main lesson: derive outputs by exact cellwise comparison of the two (or more) motif instances across demos before guessing; account for partial/missing colors, cropping, orientations, and output footprint. Prior reasoning incorrectly oscillated among color-3 masks and dimensions without evidence."
